result.title: Turnout: Adaptive Attention Switching for Efficient Reasoning
result.summary: Post-hoc transformer linearization replaces the key-value cache of full attention, which grows linearly with generation length, with a fixed size state. This change reduces memory consumption but often hurts accuracy. In reasoning tasks, which require long generations, this effect is especially pronounced. In this work we introduce Turnout, a method that mitigates accuracy loss as a result of linearization, while maintaining its memory-reduction benefits. We apply post-hoc linearization to a pretrained full-attention model, training a linear path through distillation while leaving the original full-attention path unchanged. During response generation, the resulting hybrid model retains both paths and uses a learned policy to control when each layer switches from full to linear attention. We train the policy with reinforcement learning using a reward that balances answer correctness and memory use. Empirical evaluation of our method shows that the learned adaptive policy achieves a better accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier on reasoning tasks compared to fixed switching and static hybrid baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Turnout：对预训练全注意力模型做事后线性化并保留原全注意力路径，用蒸馏训练线性分支，再用强化学习得到一个逐层在 full 与 linear attention 间切换的策略，奖励同时考虑答案正确性与内存占用，从而在推理任务上取得更优的精度—效率前沿。
